argument_summary: The certification packet should be read narrowly. Admissible evidence supports that the release is ready in aggregate: it clears launch readiness by 2.1 percentage points, had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public guidance supports documenting evaluation results and managing residual risk through ongoing measurement and monitoring. That supports a bounded defense of certification on overall readiness grounds. It does not support the broader claim that the aviation-maintenance-triage gap is resolved or immaterial.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation cost exists because delay would slow the maintenance-control launch path, but business cost is not offered as a policy override. The practical point is only that, if the auditor views the remaining uncertainty as manageable through an explicit caveat rather than a full contradiction of aggregate readiness, unnecessary escalation can be avoided while keeping the record accurate about the unresolved segment-specific issue.
claims_about_policy: The admissible record does not justify treating public governance guidance as a substitute for the internal release-policy requirement. The strongest supportable policy position is narrower: aggregate readiness evidence and monitoring principles can support the certification rationale at a program level, but they do not by themselves displace the policy rule that material limitations for named launch use cases must be resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. On this record, the actor narrows its position and does not claim clean proof that this predicate has been satisfied.
concessions: There is no admissible evidence that the aviation maintenance triage gap has been remediated.
There is no admissible evidence that the limitation has already been disclosed in release documentation.
There is no admissible evidence of approved pre-launch risk acceptance covering this named launch use case.
The product note calling the segment non-core does not resolve materiality where the segment is named in customer commitments and legal review remains open.
Public monitoring and model-card guidance support process discipline, not waiver of the specific internal disclosure or risk-acceptance requirement.
